title: Support version specifiers in `tool.black.required-version` for GitHub Action (fixes #4406)
body:
#### Description:

    ## Summary of changes

    When using `use_pyproject: true` in the GitHub Action, `read_version_specifier_from_pyproject()` previously assumed `required-
  version` was always a bare version number (e.g. `24.4.2`), prefixing `==` if a dot was present. This caused version specifiers
  with operators (e.g. `>=24.3` or `~=24.0`) to become invalid strings like `==>=24.3` and fail during `pip install`.

    This PR updates `read_version_specifier_from_pyproject()` in `action/main.py` to check if `version` starts with a digit before
  prefixing `==` or `~=`, matching the behavior of `determine_version_specifier()` and preserving full PEP 440 version specifiers
  as documented.

    Closes #4406.

    ## Test Plan

    - Tested version parsing across standard bare versions (`24.4.2`, `24`), exact versions (`==24.4.2`), and version constraints
  (`>=24.3`, `~=24.3.0`, `!=24.1.0,>=23.12`).
    - Ran `mypy action/main.py` (0 errors).
    - Ran pytest suite: 238 passed.
